newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan car imports surge to annual record.
newsitem.headline: Japan car imports surge to annual record.

text.p: Japanese motorists are buying foreign-made cars in record numbers this year, with the latest sales figures pushing the total to a new annual high even before the December figures are in.
The Japan Automobile Importers' Association (JAIA) said on Thursday that domestic sales of imported vehicles rose 4.1 percent in November from a year earlier to 35,933 units.
That brought sales of imported vehicles in the first 11 months to 389,466 vehicles, topping the 388,162 for the whole of last year.

"Sales of imported vehicles for the whole of 1996 are sure to reach 430,000 units...but will miss the initial target of 450,000 units because of poor sales of American-made Toyota and Honda cars," said Kunihiko Ono, JAIA vice-chief secretary.
Imports are expected to account for about eight percent of Japan's total 1996 vehicle sales of 5.3 to 5.4 million.
Toyota Motor Corp's unit in Kentucky stopped making the Scepter station wagon in June because of poor demand in the United States.
Industry sources said Toyota will start producing the Scepter in Japan under a different brand name from this month for sale domestically.
Honda Motor Co Ltd is expected to shift production of its popular Accord Wagon to Japan from the United States next autumn because of the shrinking U.S. market for station wagons.
The rise in November was partly due to consumers buying cars and other vehicles ahead of a consumption tax rise in Japan next April to five percent from three percent, Ono said.

U.S. automakers General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp reported strong sales in November, with sales of GM cars in Japan soaring 173 percent to 2,075, excluding those for GM's German unit Adam Opel. Sales of Chrysler cars rose 46 percent to 1,298.
Ford Motor Co's sales were sharply down, but Ono said that may have been due to consumers holding back on purchases ahead of a facelift for a couple of its more popular models.
Ford sold 954 vehicles in November, down one-third from a year earlier.

"Ford sales declined because of a facelift for its Mondeo and Explorer last month. Customers must have hesitated buying older models. I expect Ford will boost its sales in December with those new models," Ono said.
Ford launched a new right-hand-drive Mondeo station wagon and Explorer heavy sport-utility vehicle on November 26 in Japan.
Sales of German cars rose 7.8 percent last month to 15,796 units. The Volkswagen group topped the list with 5,439 cars, up 11.7 percent from a year earlier, but Mercedes and Adam Opel car sales fell.

"No worries about Mercedes and Opel sales. Both Mercedes and Opel are sold mainly by Yanase & Co (a major dealer of foreign cars). November is a preparatory month for Yanase before boosting its sales in the last month of the year," Ono said.
Sales of British cars were up 27.6 percent to 2,646 in November, Swedish cars rose 6.4 percent to 1,705 and French cars rose 13.6 percent to 743.
